title: 2 Kings 11
paragraphs: ¹ When Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she rose and destroyed the entire royal family. ² But Jehosheba, the daughter of King Joram and sister of Ahaziah, took Joash son of Ahaziah and secretly spirited him away from among the princes who were about to be murdered. She hid him and his nurse in a sleeping room in the temple of the LORD. He was concealed there from Athaliah and was not killed. ³ He remained hidden in the house of the LORD for six years while Athaliah ruled the land. ⁴ In the seventh year, Jehoiada summoned the commanders of units of a hundred, the Carites, and the guards and had them come to him at the temple of the LORD. He made a covenant with them and put them under oath there, then showed them the king's son. ⁵ He gave them these instructions: "This is what you must do: a third of you who come on duty on the Sabbath are to guard the royal palace,

⁶ a third of you are to guard the gate of Sur, and a third are to guard the gate behind the guard, and so you will keep watch over the palace in relays. ⁷ The two companies of you who go off duty on the Sabbath are to mount guard over the temple of the LORD to protect the king. ⁸ Each of you is to have his weapons in hand. You must surround the king on all sides. Anyone who approaches your ranks must be killed. Stay close to the king wherever he goes." ⁹ The commanders did everything Jehoiada the priest commanded. Each one brought his men — both those who came on duty on the Sabbath and those who went off duty — and came to Jehoiada the priest. ¹⁰ He gave the commanders the spears and shields that had belonged to King David and were kept in the temple of the LORD.

¹¹ The guards took up their positions with their weapons in hand, surrounding the king from the south side of the temple to the north side, along by the altar and the building. ¹² Then Jehoiada brought out the king's son and put the crown on him and presented him with a copy of the covenant. They proclaimed him king and anointed him, clapping their hands and shouting, "Long live the king!" ¹³ When Athaliah heard the noise of the guards and the people, she came to the people at the temple of the LORD. ¹⁴ She looked and saw the king standing by the pillar, as was the custom, with the officers and the trumpeters beside him. All the people of the land were rejoicing and blowing trumpets. Athaliah tore her robes and screamed, "Treason! Treason!" ¹⁵ Jehoiada the priest commanded the army officers: "Bring her out between the ranks, and put to the sword anyone who follows her" — for the priest had said, "She must not be killed in the temple of the LORD."

¹⁶ They seized her, and she was brought to the palace through the horses' entrance, where she was put to death. ¹⁷ Jehoiada then made a covenant between the LORD, the king, and the people that they would be the LORD's people. He also made a covenant between the king and the people. ¹⁸ All the people of the land went to the temple of Baal and demolished it. They smashed the altars and idols to pieces, and killed Mattan the priest of Baal in front of the altars. The priest also posted guards at the temple of the LORD. ¹⁹ He took the commanders of hundreds, the Carites, the guards, and all the people of the land, and they escorted the king from the temple of the LORD down through the gate of the guards to the palace. The king took his seat on the royal throne. ²⁰ All the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was calm. As for Athaliah, they had put her to death with the sword at the palace.
²¹ Jehoash was seven years old when he became king.
